title: Regeneration of TiO2 Nanotube Arrays for ESEM Analysis of Adult Pig Retina
author: Friebe, Mayr
materials: In fact, tissue residues were partially removed, but it takes much more time as for the simplified cell culture model. Furthermore, we see an increase in free salt deposits with increasing UV exposure time.

TiO2 nanotubes were produced by electrochemical anodization at room temperature. In doing so, titanium foil (Advent Research Materials Ltd., 0.1 mm thickness, 99.6 + % purity) was first cut in the desired size, for our experiments with retinal tissue 20 mm × 30 mm, cleaned by ultrasonication each for 10 min in distilled water and isopropyl alcohol and dried in a nitrogen stream. Cut and cleaned titanium foil served as anode and a platinum-mesh as cathode. Both electrodes were fixed with a constant distance of 45 mm. Titanium-foil was chemically etched by immersing both electrodes into electrolyte (consisting of 98% ethylene glycol, 2% distilled water and 0.3% ammonium fluoride powder) and anodized for 60 min. For experiments with the murine L929 cell line, size of scaffolds was chosen as 10 mm × 10 mm. An anodization voltage of 16 V was used leading to nanotubes with a diameter of d = (32 ± 3) nm, which were suitable for single cell culturing [7]. For experiments with retinal tissue an anodization voltage of 50 V was used which leads to a tube diameter of d = (72 ± 3) nm [10]. Each anodized TiO2 nanotube array was cleaned with ethylene glycole, gently dried with nitrogen stream and afterwards in furnace at 42 °C overnight. To complete nanotube production and to make them usable for single cell culturing, a final cleaning step was performed in an ultrasonic bath with distilled water for 10°min to ensure a complete removal of all electrolyte residues.

ESEM analyses were all carried out with a Quanta FEG scanning electron microscope (FEI Munich, Germany) which has three operating vacuum modes: high vacuum, low vacuum and ESEM (environmental). Furthermore, an EDX (energy dispersive X-ray) spectroscope is included in our ESEM setup. ESEM analyses were performed to investigate adhesion of individual cells grown on top of nanotube surfaces to ensure cell adherence and to check for remaining residues originating from tissue cultivation. After that, distinct cleaning methods were tested for retinal tissue residues as well. To analyze residues and cleaning effects, high vacuum mode was used for imaging. For ESEM-mode analyses, nanotube arrays with living cells on top were mounted into a special holder in which 4–5 droplets of distilled water were filled. Measurement started immediately and lasted up to 2 h maximum. Humidity and temperature were set to 40–70% and 4–8 °C, while pressure varied from 400 to 700 Pa. After completing ESEM-measurements of L929 cells cultured on top of nanotube arrays, samples were fixed with 4% PFA and some of them were stained for fluorescent microscopy while others were dried in furnace at 42 °C overnight for residual analysis. Samples were cleaned with UV-light or O2-plasma for different durations, as described in next chapter. ESEM analysis was continued without any washing steps in-between to make sure that cleaning effect came solely from the cleaning method. Cleaning procedure and measurements were repeated until no changes on residues could be detected or the surface was completely free of debris. The same preparation conditions as for single cells were applied for tissue residues on top of nanotube arrays: samples were fixed with 2% GA and 2% PFA, some samples were used for fluorescent microscopy to confirm presence of rods and cones while other samples were dried overnight and used for different cleaning procedures.
The datasets used and analysed during the current study are available from the corresponding author.

steps.title: Synthesize TiO2 nanotube arrays
steps.instruction: Cut Ti foil (0.1 mm, 99.6 %+ purity, Advent Research Materials) to the required size (20 mm × 30 mm for retina, 10 mm × 10 mm for cell work), ultrasonicate 10 min in distilled water then 10 min in isopropyl alcohol, dry with N₂, mount as anode opposite a Pt‑mesh cathode 45 mm away, prepare electrolyte (98 % ethylene glycol, 2 % distilled water, 0.3 % NH₄F), anodize 60 min at 16 V (cell arrays, d = 32 ± 3 nm) or 50 V (retina arrays, d = 72 ± 3 nm), rinse with ethylene glycol, dry with N₂, furnace‑dry at 42 °C overnight, finish with a 10 min ultrasonic bath in distilled water.

steps.title: Seed L929 fibroblasts on arrays
steps.instruction: Grow L929 cells in a 75 cm² flask, passage at 80 % confluence, then add 10 000 cells to each 1 cm² nanotube array placed in a 48‑well plate (each well 1 cm²). Allow cells to settle for 2 h at 37 °C, 100 % humidity, 5 % CO₂, then add 1.5 ml medium per well (48‑well) and 3 ml medium per array (RPMI 90 % + 10 % FCS + 0.1 % gentamycin). Culture up to 7 days, changing medium every third day.

steps.title: Fix and dry cell samples
steps.instruction: After the desired culture period (1, 4 or 7 days) image the live cells by ESEM, then fix with 4 % paraformaldehyde for 24 h, and dry overnight in a vacuum‑assisted furnace (≈42 °C).

steps.title: UV‑irradiate cell‑covered arrays
steps.instruction: Place the PFA‑fixed, dried arrays in a UV chamber flushed with N₂, use a 172 nm/630 Z lamp (16 mW cm⁻²) positioned 26 mm from the sample. Irradiate for a total of 102 min (dose ≈ 96 J cm⁻²), acquiring high‑vacuum ESEM images after 0, 2, 22, 62 and 102 min at the same position.

steps.title: O₂‑plasma treat cell samples
steps.instruction: Insert the PFA‑fixed, dried arrays into an O₂‑plasma chamber, evacuate and flush with O₂, then expose to 100 % O₂‑plasma for a total of 45 min. Acquire ESEM images after 5 min, 30 min and 45 min to monitor residue removal.

steps.title: Prepare adult pig retina explants
steps.instruction: Obtain pig eyes (6–7 months, 100–150 kg) from a slaughterhouse, stun and bleed, remove eyes within 2 h, place in chilled PBS (4 °C). Under sterile conditions open the globe, detach vitreous, separate retina from RPE with tweezers, cut to ≈0.8 cm² pieces.

steps.title: Culture retina on nanotube arrays
steps.instruction: Place each retina piece photoreceptor‑side down on a TiO₂ nanotube array (30 mm × 30 mm × 5 mm stainless‑steel grid) inside a petri dish. Add Ames medium containing 0.1 % gentamycin and 10 % horse serum so that the liquid contacts the underside of the array but does not cover the top, creating a thin wetting layer. Incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 7 or 14 days.

steps.title: Fix and remove retina tissue
steps.instruction: After culture, fix the retina in situ with 2 % glutaraldehyde + 2 % paraformaldehyde (GA/PFA) for overnight (≈24 h), then gently detach the tissue using a soft brush and pipette.

steps.title: UV‑irradiate tissue‑covered arrays
steps.instruction: Place the GA/PFA‑fixed, dried retina‑residue arrays in the same UV chamber (172 nm, 16 mW cm⁻², 26 mm distance). Irradiate for up to 15 h, acquiring ESEM images after 0, 1, 2, 3, 7 and 15 h to assess cleaning progress.

steps.title: O₂‑plasma treat tissue samples
steps.instruction: Insert the fixed, dried retina‑residue arrays into the O₂‑plasma chamber, flush with O₂ and expose to 100 % O₂‑plasma for a total of 145 min. Record ESEM images after 25, 85 and 145 min to monitor residue removal.

steps.title: Enzymatic cleaning with lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare 100 ml lysis buffer stock: 10 ml 100 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.5, 1 ml 5 mM EDTA, 1 ml 0.2 % SDS, 4 ml 200 mM NaCl, 84 ml distilled water. Add Proteinase K to a final concentration of 0.5 mg ml⁻¹ immediately before use. Incubate the retina‑residue arrays in this buffer at 55 °C for 24 h in a furnace, then wash the substrates several times with PBS.

steps.title: Final washing and storage
steps.instruction: After enzymatic treatment, rinse the cleaned nanotube arrays repeatedly with PBS, dry briefly with N₂ if needed, and store in a clean, dry container until reuse.

steps.title: ESEM imaging of samples
steps.instruction: Mount samples in the ESEM holder. For live‑cell imaging add 4–5 droplets of distilled water, set humidity 40–70 %, temperature 4–8 °C, pressure 400–700 Pa, and acquire images within 2 h. For fixed samples use high‑vacuum mode after drying. No washing steps are performed between cleaning and imaging to ensure observed changes are due to the cleaning method.

steps.title: Calculate cell doubling time
steps.instruction: Capture daily bright‑field images of cells on nanotube arrays and on control dishes, count cells with ImageJ, and compute doubling time using N = N₀ e^{kt} (t = time, k = growth constant).
